thread:
maya: FYI — Acme reported a subtle change after the model bump this morning (v2.3.1 -> v2.4.0). They say replies are shorter and drop hedging/greeting lines. Pasting the customer examples below. Can we repro quickly?

sam: Can you attach the exact prompts + responses from the customer? also need model id and time of issue.

maya: Copied from their ticket: 
```
Prompt: "Summarize our release notes for customers in friendly language."
Response (before): "Hi! Here are the key points from the release: ... We recommend ..."
Response (after): "Release highlights: ... Recommend ..."
```
They said tone feels more blunt and sentences are denser. No explicit content change, just phrasing.

jordan: Interesting. Do we know rollout strategy for v2.4.0? was it canary-first?

lee: v2.4.0 was rolled at 03:10 UTC with a 20% canary, then 100% at 03:40 after no error alerts.

sam: Thanks — quick checklist: 1) confirm no system prompt change pushed to customers, 2) check model config (temperature, top_p, repetition_penalty), 3) compare average output token count pre/post, 4) fetch inference logs for one of the request IDs the customer attached.

maya: They included request id: req_0b4f9c2a. Attached screenshots in ticket.

evan: I'll pull logs. (running query)

ops-bot: Log query started for req_0b4f9c2a -> trace: a1f7d0. Estimated 4s.

evan: Found it — model: redwood-v2.4.0, temp: 0.3, top_p: 0.95, max_tokens: 160, stop: ["\n\n"]. Output tokens: 28, previously avg for same prompt ~ 42 tokens.

sam: 28 vs 42 — that's measurable. Could be shorter decoding due to changed eos bias or updated tokenizer/stripping. Any quantization changes in v2.4.0?

jordan: v2.4.0 included a small eos-logit fix to reduce hallucinated continuations. That change might raise probability of early termination in some prompts.

lee: Hmm, we shipped an eos penalty adjustment and a tokenization normalization tweak. Both intended to reduce extra words, but could make responses terser.

maya: Customer wants style preserved. They flagged it as a regression in tone. They are asking for a short-term mitigation.

sam: Short-term options: 1) temporarily route Acme to v2.3.1 (rollback for that customer), 2) add a post-prompt instruction to enforce friendliness (system or user-level), 3) tweak decoding (raise temperature slightly or disable eos tweak for that customer). Which is easiest?

evan: Easiest is per-customer routing to v2.3.1 — takes minutes if customer on Dedicated/Dedicated-like routing. For hosted API, we can pin API key to older version in the control plane for them.

jordan: Also recommend we reproduce locally with a small script: curl example below — run both versions and diff token counts and BLEU-like similarity on phrasing.

sam: Example repro curl: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2.4.0","input":"Summarize our release notes for customers in friendly language.","temperature":0.3,"max_tokens":160}'
```
Run same with redwood-v2.3.1 and compare outputs.

maya: I'll ask acct mgmt if pinning is acceptable for Acme (they're on an enterprise plan). Also asking for a couple more prompt examples from their product docs to ensure cover.

evan: Quick note from logs: there is a slight increase in EOS logit bias post-deploy (+0.6 avg on sample prompts). That aligns with shorter outputs.

lee: Ok — eng-ml action items: (1) quantify eos bias change across 500 sample prompts, (2) test re-decoding with eos tweak off, (3) measure perceived friendliness via our tiny sentiment heuristic.

jordan: I'll own the behavioral test. Can someone grant me access to the rollback toggle for hosted routing?

sam: I can do the pin for Acme if we get greenlight from acct mgmt.

maya: Acct team says yes to temporary pin. Please do it and also feed the customer a short note: "We've pinned you to v2.3.1 while we investigate. Expect no change in latency/usage."

evan: Pin applied for API key acct-acme-77 -> now routed to redwood-v2.3.1. Confirmed via logs: next requests hitting v2.3.1.

maya: Thanks all. Jordan/Lee/Evan — please post findings by EOD. I'll update the customer and set expectation that engineering is investigating a decoding/eos-related phrasing shift.

sam: Quick follow-up: let's capture a before/after snippet in the ticket and include model cfg diff. That will help quality/regression alerts.

maya: Will do — closing loop after eng posts results. :thumbsup:
